relevance.rationale: Mironov-Morozov on a 'combinatorial Borel transform': averaging Cauchy identities for Schur functions over the power-sum variables p_k, which rescales the combinatorial factors (d_R and the like) in sums over Young diagrams the way the ordinary exponential Borel transform rescales factorials, thereby unifying a collection of previously scattered single-Schur-sum identities and their skew-Schur counterparts. Two superficially matching corpus vocabularies do not in fact match. (i) The corpus's Borel front is resurgent -- the Borel transform of an asymptotic series in hbar = log q, its plane singularities and Stokes structure -- not a reweighting of diagram sums. (ii) The corpus's Young-diagram object is the fixed-n Frobenius pairing tr_M = sum_{lambda |- n} y_lambda chi^lambda over the Wedderburn blocks of H_n(q), and Delta_lambda = (-1)^{n(lambda)} dim V_lambda; the identities here are generating sums over ALL diagrams, with no fixed-n truncation and no q-deformation of the Hecke kind. I could not name a corpus place that wants one of these identities, so per the skill the key-results list is empty. Scope-(a): as read, nothing usable; averaged-Schur techniques are not thereby excluded from the covariance-kernel front.

proposedActions.rationale: Adjacent vocabulary only. If anyone does want to revisit it, the relevant prior assessment of diagram-sum literature against the corpus's covariance-kernel obstruction is the 2026-07-24 literature assessment, which this paper was not part of.
